D022_l001.question:
A 26-year-old single female, employed as a kindergarten teacher, presents with a 6-month history of recurrent episodes of eating an objectively large amount of food in a discrete time period, accompanied by a subjective sense of loss of control over eating during these episodes. These episodes occur, on average, more than once per week and are associated with significant distress. To prevent weight gain, the patient engages in recurrent compensatory behaviors, including self-induced vomiting and intermittent fasting. These behaviors are not associated with anorexia nervosa and occur in the absence of another medical or psychiatric condition that would otherwise account for this pattern.

The patient exhibits marked preoccupation with body weight and shape, with an intense fear of gaining weight despite being within a normal weight range. Her self-evaluation is unduly influenced by her perception of her body shape and weight, and she reports that her sense of personal worth is heavily contingent upon her physical appearance. There is no evidence of concurrent binge-purge behavior secondary to another eating disorder type. Symptoms have persisted for the past six months, with the compensatory behaviors and binge episodes occurring regularly throughout this time, meeting frequency and duration criteria for clinical significance.
D022_l001.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
